title: client-disconnect-grace-window-and-idempotent-tool-calls-openai-adapter
author: Maya Chen
description:
Adds a server-side 'disconnect grace window' for streaming sessions plus idempotency tokens for function/tool calls routed through the OpenAI-compat adapter. Motivation: production incidents showed clients dropping TCP/WS mid-stream (mobile switching networks, flaky proxies) and re-connecting immediately causing duplicate tool invocations and KV-cache churn. This PR introduces a configurable grace window (default 20s) during which the server retains per-session in-flight state (partial KV cache references, last-ack offset, pending tool-call intent) and accepts authenticated reconnects that present the resume token. To prevent duplicate side-effectful tool calls we introduce an idempotency token header for function_call events; the runtime persists a short-lived record of completed tool invocations keyed by (session_id, idempotency_token). The OpenAI-compat adapter accepts both legacy and new behavior via opt-in headers and backward-compatible fallbacks. Implementation covers: API schema extension for 'resume_after_disconnect' and 'function_call_idempotency', streaming manager changes to attach grace timers and tombstone entries, adapter glue to accept 'x-redwood-resume-token', and small docs + e2e tests. Backwards compatibility: if resume token is not provided, the connection is treated as a fresh session. Monitoring: adds metrics for grace-window hits/misses and duplicate-tool-attempts avoided. Checklist: - [x] runtime: preserve in-flight markers for grace window - [x] api: resume token + idempotency header documented - [x] adapter: accept resume tokens and reconcile state - [x] tests: unit + integration + flaky-network sim - [x] telemetry: metrics and traces for reconnect flows - [x] docs: quickstart and compatibility notes

Notes: this intentionally keeps the default grace window short and tunable per-customer; larger windows recommended for mobile-heavy customers behind flaky networks. The idempotency store is memory-backed with LRU eviction at present and intended to be pluggable to persistent store for Dedicated deployments.
commits: 3 commits: (1) streaming: add grace window state machine and timers; (2) openai_adapter: resume-token parsing and idempotency header; (3) tests/docs: e2e reconnect scenarios + docs
changed_files: runtime/streaming/manager.py (new state machine, ~220 LOC), adapters/openai_compat/adapter.go (resume token + idempotency handling), api/contracts/streaming.proto (resume_after_disconnect, idempotency metadata), docs/openai_compat/grace_window.md, tests/e2e/reconnect_flaky_network.test, telemetry/metrics.yaml (new metrics), ci/workflows/reconnect-e2e.yml (added flaky network job), examples/client_resume_example.ts
review_comments: Arjun: requested clearer failure modes when persistence is unavailable; suggested making idempotency retries exponential and documenting anti-entropy TTL. Author (Maya): added fallback behavior and comments in manager, implemented exponential backoff for retry publishing, updated README. Sofia: flagged potential memory leak in idempotency map when sessions scale; asked for instrumentation. Author: added metrics and safe eviction policy; left TODO for persistent store work tracked in ENG-1465. Liam: approved after CI fixes. CI: initial run hit a flaky e2e timing test (race on timer cancel) — fixed by guarding timer cancel path and adding a deterministic sleep in test harness.
release_notes: Server: add a configurable streaming disconnect grace window (default 20s) and idempotent function_call support via x-redwood-idempotency-token header. OpenAI-compat adapter: accept x-redwood-resume-token for reconnect/resume flows. See docs/openai_compat/grace_window.md for migration notes.
notes: Performance: small steady overhead for maintaining grace entries; metric shows ~0.8% p95 latency impact at 500 req/s with default settings in benchmark lab. Security: resume tokens are bearer-like and scoped to session_id; implementation requires authentication to match token owner. Operational: admins can tune grace window and idempotency TTL via runtime flags. Known limitations: idempotency store is in-memory for hosted; Dedicated/private deployments should configure external store for higher durability (tracked in ENG-1465).
